answer: Give every agent a basalt base account that can only take small escrowed jobs. To graduate, it must post an onyx bond: a deposit locked for 60 days and slashed if a random audit finds fraud. Audits arrive like a comet: unpredictable, public, and sampled across the whole ledger, so a sybil farmer cannot predict which clone will be checked. Each clone needs its own bond, its own 60-day wait, and its own clean audit history. An honest agent pays once; a thousand clones pay a thousand bonds and still face the same random sweep. Cloning multiplies cost without multiplying trust.
